title: Ticket stock
rule: Told on a strip of railway card tickets, one beat per ticket, dated, numbered and punched.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
made: a strip of six card tickets, HANDMADE cut paper (cutpaper99.Cut: scissor-faceted card, the LoC 1934 sheet's fibre as tone, one down-right shadow; card grain held at 0.55 for the file-size target), six card colours, joined at rows of round perforation holes

each ticket printed in the shared pen hand: a stub with 'No.', the big ticket number 1-6 and a serial (Ser. 3701-3706) behind a perforated divider; 'CENTRAL VERMONT RY.  RANDOLPH, VT.'; a route line (DESK to CUPBOARD / STOP: TICKET WINDOW / CLOCK: 4:10 / RETURN: PLATFORM / ARRIVAL: CUPBOARD / NOT GOOD FOR: SERVICE DOOR); the beat in two lines with the canon memo text and the four lines verbatim; small print 'Good for this afternoon only. Not transferable.'
dated: a violet dater-stamp oval on each ticket, 'SEP 1937' and the minute (4:09, 4:10, 4:10, 4:10, 4:11, 4:11 PM), uneven ink; the clock reads 4:10 at the answer, before the memo's 4:15
punched: a conductor's clipper hole cut through each ticket's stub (the sheet shows through, the hole's edge shadowed)

a small cut-paper picture on each ticket, re-cut from page 16's cut-paper figure kit (p16_fewest_marks: agent, stranger, clock, ticket window, cupboard opening on its left jamb, key with SERVICE tag, SERVICE door, memo, desk); folio '33 / Ticket stock' (pen99.folio); ticket 4's picture re-cut: the window's middle stands empty, the stranger small and far with her back turned, half gone behind the right post on her way down the platform, and the agent turned back toward the cupboard, walking left

events.E0: ticket 1 (4:09): DESK to CUPBOARD, the memo, he sets off
events.E1: ticket 2 (4:10): STOP: TICKET WINDOW, the question
events.E4: ticket 5 (4:11): ARRIVAL: CUPBOARD, the key on its hook, tag SERVICE
events.E5: ticket 6 (4:11): NOT GOOD FOR: SERVICE DOOR, the forgetting line; key stays, door shut

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the strip is issued ticket by ticket, each one clipped (punched) as the next is laid

self_check.check: A reader reads the tickets in number order (1-6, top to bottom) and finds E0-E5 (maker's judgement from the full-size page; blind reading pending)

ticket2_vs_ticket4.t2: facing the office at the centre of the window, scale 0.44
ticket2_vs_ticket4.t4: back turned, scale 0.27, at the right post

weaknesses: the pictures are small at phone width (about 400 px on the page); the text on each ticket carries the beat
in ticket 4 she is still visible at the edge of the glass (receding) rather than gone
repairs: repair 2026-11-17 (batch 3): ticket 4 vignette re-cut (she leaves: window centre empty, she recedes behind the post; agent turned to the cupboard)
